---
title: "known_issues"
output: html_document
---

- `scatter_3d` has not been rigorously tested

- `lm`'s with data accessed by `$` (ie `lm(mtcars$mpg ~ mtcars$disp)`) are currently not allowed (`geom_slice` and `slice_2d` both reject them with a clear error). This should be extended to all accessed variables (ie `mtcars['mpg']`) because of how they are handled in the `predict` function. When this is fixed, `decisions.Rmd` should be updated.

- `SliceLayer` in `geom_slice.R` inherits from `ggplot2:::Layer` via `:::` because ggplot2 (4.0.3) does not export the `Layer` class even though `layer(layer_class = ...)` is the documented extension point. Harmless at runtime, but `R CMD check` will note the use of an unexported object. If ggplot2 ever exports `Layer`, drop the `:::`.

- `geom_slice` grouping is recovered from *visible* aesthetics (`color`, `linetype`, ...). A bare `group = var` aesthetic cannot pin `var` per group — ggplot2 reduces group values to opaque integer ids before the stat runs — so `geom_slice` warns and holds the variable constant instead. (Covered by a warning, not silent; see `resolve_y_fn`/`build_slice_spec` in `R/geom_slice.R`.)

- In composite-axis mode (an x-axis *expression* like `aes(x * x_pos, y)`), the line is evaluated at the model's own data points rather than an `n`-point grid, so `n` is ignored there. Also, the plotted "line" is only guaranteed to be a clean curve when the model's predictions are a function of the axis expression (true for the `gs_19`–`gs_23` family); otherwise points would not be collinear against that axis and the connected line can zigzag — arguably the honest picture, but worth knowing.

- (noted 2026-08-18) A projection band is resolved **twice**, at two different times, by design. `build_slice_spec()` resolves it at *build* time, when the layout and the fully-inherited mapping exist; `geom_slice_subtitle()` (to describe the band) and `geom_slice_text()` (to label its edges) both need the banded variable earlier, at *add* time, and neither can wait for the build. Both go through the same `resolve_slice_band()` via the shared `slice_add_time_context()` / `slice_layer_band()` helpers in `R/geom_slice.R`, so the inference rules exist once — but the *inputs* are reconstructed from the plot object as it stands when the layer is added, and a facet, a layer-level `aes()`, or a `%+%` data swap added *after* the slice layer can make the two answers disagree. Build time stays authoritative for what is drawn, so a disagreement shows up as a wrong or missing label / subtitle line on a correct plot, never a wrong band. The add-time calls pass `quiet = TRUE` and swallow errors, so warnings fire once, at build time. Not yet observed in practice — every case adds facets before the slice layer, which is also what the docs show. If ggplot2 ever offers a hook between "plot is complete" and "plot is built", both consumers should move there and this note can go.

- (noted 2026-08-18) An invalid `style` through `geom_slice_subtitle(...)` warns and falls back to `"prettier"`, but `annotation_equation_args()` has already read it as a pinned style and dropped the `"brackets"` wrap fallback, so the subtitle can run off a narrow plot. Detecting it would put `style` validation back inside the annotation, which is what `...` exists to avoid — and the warning names the typo, which is the fix.

## Resolved

- ~~`geom_slice_text(expand = TRUE)` replaced the plot's x scale~~ — resolved 2026-08-19. `ggplot_add.slice_text_spec` now edits the expansion on the scale the plot already has (`set_scale_expand` in `R/geom_slice_text.R`, on a clone of `plot$scales`), so a user's `scale_x_*()` keeps its limits, breaks, name and transform and ggplot2 no longer emits "Scale for x is already present". A plot that named no scale has no scale object to edit — its default does not exist until build time — so the one the probe build settled on is added instead, which is what keeps a defaulted Date or log axis intact. An expansion the user set on the side away from the labels is now read off that scale rather than assumed to be ggplot2's 5%, and any additive expansion is carried through. Cases `gt_18` (user `scale_x_continuous` with limits/breaks/name) and `gt_19` (`scale_x_log10()`).

- ~~`devtools::load_all()` warned "replacing previous import" three times (plotly vs graphics/ggplot2/stats)~~ — resolved 2026-07-12 by narrowing the blanket `@import` tags to `@importFrom` (only `plot_ly`/`add_markers`/`add_trace`/`layout` are imported from plotly now, and `graphics::layout`, `ggplot2::last_plot`, `stats::filter` are not imported at all).

## Resolved (2026-07-07 geom_slice overhaul — see for_devs/geom_slice_progress.Rmd)

- ~~`geom_slice` used `names(model$model)` for variable handling~~ — now uses the formula + `get_all_vars()`, so `lm(y ~ I(x^2))` etc. resolve to raw variables.
- ~~`detect_response_transform` vastly inferior to `get_inverse_function`~~ — `detect_response_transform` is gone; `geom_slice` now uses `get_inverse_function`.
- ~~`SliceLayer` inherited from a Layer *instance*~~ — now a proper `Layer` subclass passed via `layer(layer_class = ...)` (the fix recommended in `ggplot_layer_internals.Rmd`), which is what made grouping and faceting work.
